summary.headline: BlueStone Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 49.1% YoY; SSG of 34% and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with 340 stores after 65 added in FY26.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 49.1% YoY and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with same-store sales growth of 34% spread evenly across all three months. The store base reached 340 stores in 134 cities after adding 17 stores in Q4 and 65 in FY26, below the 83 added in FY25 and below the RHP plan of 290 stores over FY26-FY27. Management said pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improved YoY despite a mix shift toward plain gold, and attributed the recovery to rapid entry-level repricing and vertical integration. Gold price inflation inflated closing inventory, which pushed inventory turns down to about 1.13x from 1.3x in FY25.

segments.name: Company-operated stores
segments.commentary: 340 stores across 134 cities at March 2026, with about 67 franchisee-owned stores; franchisee stores are being wound down in FY27-FY28 and the 5-year contracts are being honoured.

segments.name: Men's and kids' jewellery store format
segments.commentary: Management described a first-of-its-kind exclusive store for men's and kids' jewellery as a test of extending the product width; no revenue or performance figures were given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to keep adding about 20% to store count annually (about 65 stores in FY26 vs 83 in FY25), calling it a tactical call tied to gold-price-driven demand conviction.
Management said Q4 SSSG of 34% reflects a return to normal, and exit momentum into FY27 is strong; no specific March exit number or FY27/FY28 revenue target was given.
Management expects a substantial drop in franchisee-owned company-operated stores in FY27 and FY28, while honouring the 5-year franchise contracts.
A&P will be held at about 6% of revenue, with absolute spend rising and a shift from performance marketing toward brand building.
Management expects inventory efficiency to improve if gold prices remain stable over the next year.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 17 in Q4 FY26, 65 in FY26, against 83 in FY25; target of close to 20% distribution growth each year.
Long-term economics target: mature stores are expected to converge to at least INR 14-15 crore revenue per store at peak utilisation (analyst's question, management said 'at the minimum').
Store sizing: management is opening larger stores (for example 2,000 sq ft rather than 1,200 sq ft) to cut relocation risk; no store closures in FY26, with relocations counted separately.
Manufacturing: operating leverage from capacity utilisation came through in FY25-FY26, but manufacturing still carries an element of fixed cost.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 34% in Q4 FY26, consistent across all three months; management says SSSG is not skewed toward newer stores.
Gold price moved close to 100% over the past 15-18 months, with the sharpest rises in Q2-Q3 FY25 when SSSG was lowest.
Entry-level range was repriced quickly using the vertically integrated model; management did not quantify its revenue contribution.
Share of gold sales has fallen to about 55% of revenue (analyst's figure); management said FY26 exit mix is close to 60% gold, with quarterly variation driven by gold prices.
Management says plain gold and diamond are additive and priced at a premium; it denies that plain gold is dilutive to ROCE.
Management expects consumer demand to return strongly once gold prices consolidate.

qa_highlights.question: Franchisee store count and plan for them?
qa_highlights.answer: About 67 of 340 stores are franchisee-owned; the model was used as a capital structure tool, and FY27-FY28 should see a substantial drop as contracts (5 years) run down.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory turns fall from about 1.3x to 1.13x despite fewer store adds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to a one-off rise in closing inventory value from gold prices. Mature stores (3-4+ years) run at 1.7x-1.9x turns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the store plan been cut from 290 in the RHP to 65 in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slowdown was a tactical call tied to gold-price demand conviction, and Q4 added 17 stores, a pickup. It reaffirmed about 20% annual distribution growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 34% SSSG sustainable as stores mature?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY20 SSSG was near 30%, Q2-Q3 FY25 was the anomaly from the gold spike, and Q4 is a return to normal. Growth is spread across old and new cohorts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall QoQ and YoY on mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY is the right comparison because costs are largely fixed; pre-Ind AS margin improved YoY despite the mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin hold if plain gold keeps rising in mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said plain gold is additive, not substitutive, premium pricing holds, and operating leverage will expand EBITDA and capital productivity; it declined to give a numeric offset.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ESOP cost up about 80%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ESOPs are a management-only plan (about 90% held by the top six), 50-60% granted pre-IPO, with front-loaded accounting charges of INR 93 crore, then 58, then 28 crore; unallocated pool is about 1.7%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no forward-looking revenue guidance.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility: it drives closing inventory value, inventory turns, the MTM effect on customer gold schemes, and gross margin mix.
Inventory turns declined to about 1.13x and GMROI is falling; management says the decline is partly one-off and expects recovery if gold stays stable.
Store expansion pace has been cut versus the RHP plan (290 stores over FY26-FY27); watch whether FY27 store adds reach about 20%.
Franchisee exit in FY27-FY28 will shift the store mix to company-operated stores and change capital structure.
Other current liabilities rose to INR 1,001 crore (customer advances, schemes, gift vouchers); a sharper rise in gold could lift this further.
ESOP charge is front-loaded and is expected to fall to INR 28 crore in the third year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and store economics, with defensive answers on inventory turns, margin mix and store-plan cuts, which were attributed to gold prices and one-off factors. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance or numeric targets for entry-level contribution.
key_quotes: Same-store sales growth of 34% this quarter demonstrates that demand environment is resilient.
So 34% is not something which is very new for us.
So from a ROCE perspective, it's not that plain gold is dilutive to ROCE and diamond is significantly accretive, right?
